subproblems.title: Jacobian minors of Lipschitz maps are Borel measurable and uniformly bounded (reused accepted lemma; supplied Notation and step 1)
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ and L ∈ ℝ≥0, let g_c : ℝ^k → ℝ (c ∈ Fin r) be L-Lipschitz, and let V_b ∈ ℝ^k (b ∈ Fin r), where ℝ^k = Euclid k. Put D(x) := det(Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin r} (row c, column b), where Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x is the zero map at points where g is not differentiable. Then x ↦ D(x) is Borel measurable, and |D(x)| ≤ r!·(L·Σ_{b ∈ Fin r} ‖V_b‖)^r for every x ∈ ℝ^k. (Reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_minor_measurable_bound, whose frozen type is byte-identical.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (g : Fin r → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin r → Euclid k), (∀ c, LipschitzWith L (g c)) → Measurable (fun x => Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b))) ∧ ∀ x, |Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b))| ≤ (r.factorial : ℝ) * ((L : ℝ) * ∑ b, ‖V b‖) ^ r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the supplied proof ("It is Borel in u (measurable_fderiv), and |D_t v^i(u)| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ v u‖ ≤ L everywhere (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz)"; "By the Leibniz formula, |M^{a,b}(v)| ≤ K_r := r!·L^r everywhere") and its step 1. It is stated for arbitrary scalar L-Lipschitz rows g_c and arbitrary directions V_b. For the coordinate rows g_c = v^{a(c)} and the directions V_t = e_{b(t)} the bound reads r!·(L·r)^r; it plays the role of K_r, since the supplied argument only needs some uniform bound. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_minor_measurable_bound (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.minor_bound-a1, candidate commit 13966862f4c84217ad5d35ba66b3e5440c90d946), reused with a byte-identical frozen type, so no new formal work is needed. The argument is the following.

Notation: e_{c,b}(x) := Dg_c(x)V_b is the (c, b) entry; s := L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖ ≥ 0.

1. (Measurable entries.) For each c the map x ↦ Dg_c(x), from ℝ^k to the complete normed space of continuous linear maps ℝ^k → ℝ, is Borel measurable; this holds for every function (Mathlib measurable_fderiv). Evaluation T ↦ T V_b is continuous, so each entry x ↦ e_{c,b}(x) is measurable (measurable_fderiv_apply_const).
2. (Measurability of D.) By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), D(x) = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin r)} sign(σ)·Π_{b ∈ Fin r} e_{σ(b),b}(x). This is a finite sum of constants times finite products of the measurable functions of step 1, so D is measurable.
3. (Entry bound.) An L-Lipschitz g satisfies ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ L at every x. At a differentiability point the derivative of an L-Lipschitz function has operator norm at most L, and elsewhere Dg(x) = 0 (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence |e_{c,b}(x)| ≤ ‖Dg_c(x)‖·‖V_b‖ ≤ L·‖V_b‖ ≤ L·Σ_{b'} ‖V_{b'}‖ = s, all summands being nonnegative.
4. (Determinant bound.) By step 2, the triangle inequality, |sign σ| = 1 and step 3, |D(x)| ≤ Σ_σ Π_b |e_{σ(b),b}(x)| ≤ Σ_σ s^r = r!·s^r, since Perm(Fin r) has r! elements (Fintype.card_perm). For r = 0 this reads |1| ≤ 1. This is the claimed bound, valid at every x.
proof_key_steps: Each entry x ↦ Dg_c(x)V_b is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv).
Leibniz formula: the determinant is a finite signed sum of products of entries, hence measurable.
‖Dg_c(x)‖ ≤ L everywhere gives |entries| ≤ L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖.
Leibniz and the triangle inequality give |det| ≤ r!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^r.

subproblems.title: Reduction from L¹ weights to smooth compactly supported weights for uniformly bounded sequences (reused accepted lemma; supplied step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ and C ∈ ℝ, and let F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) and F : ℝ^k → ℝ be a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to Lebesgue measure λ on ℝ^k = Euclid k, with |F_j(x)| ≤ C and |F(x)| ≤ C for all j and all x. Suppose that ∫ ψ·F_j dλ → ∫ ψ·F dλ as j → ∞ for every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ with compact support (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ, the smooth class ∞, and HasCompactSupport ψ). Then ∫ φ·F_j dλ → ∫ φ·F dλ as j → ∞ for every λ-integrable φ : ℝ^k → ℝ. (Reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_weak_star_l1_upgrade, whose frozen type is byte-identical.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof ("Reduction to smooth compactly supported weights ... |∫ c M^{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ c M^{a,b}(v₀)| ≤ |∫ φ M^{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ φ M^{a,b}(v₀)| + 4K_r ε"), stated for an arbitrary uniformly bounded sequence. The sibling coordinate_minor_continuity uses it with F_j, F the minors of the approximating and the limit rows and C the bound of the sibling minor_bound. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_weak_star_l1_upgrade (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.weak_star_l1_upgrade-a1, candidate commit 7ba02a03145b060d32f1724fe453e480c4209154), reused with a byte-identical frozen type, so no new formal work is needed. The argument is the following.

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; ‖θ‖₁ := ∫ |θ| dλ.

1. (Sign of C; basic estimate.) C ≥ |F(0)| ≥ 0. Let θ be integrable and let G be a.e.-strongly measurable with |G(x)| ≤ C for all x. Then θ·G is integrable (Integrable.mul_bdd) and |∫ θG dλ| ≤ ∫ |θ|·|G| dλ ≤ C·‖θ‖₁.
2. (Choice of η.) Fix ε > 0 and put η := ε/(4C + 1) > 0. Then C·η < ε/4, because 4C < 4C + 1.
3. (Density of C_c^∞ in L¹.) There is a C^∞ function ψ with compact support and ‖φ − ψ‖₁ ≤ η. First choose a continuous compactly supported φ₁ with ‖φ − φ₁‖₁ ≤ η/2: continuous compactly supported functions are dense in L¹(λ), λ being a regular measure on ℝ^k (Mathlib Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). Then let 0 < δ ≤ 1, let ρ_δ ≥ 0 be a C^∞ kernel with ∫ ρ_δ dλ = 1 vanishing outside the ball B(0, δ) (a normalized bump function), and put ψ_δ(x) := ∫ ρ_δ(t)·φ₁(x − t) dλ(t). ψ_δ is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left) and vanishes outside the compact set K₁ := {x : dist(x, spt φ₁) ≤ 1}. Moreover |ψ_δ(x) − φ₁(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_δ(t)·|φ₁(x − t) − φ₁(x)| dλ(t) ≤ w(δ), where w(δ) := sup{|φ₁(y) − φ₁(y')| : |y − y'| ≤ δ}. Since φ₁ is continuous with compact support, it is uniformly continuous, so w(δ) → 0 as δ → 0. As ψ_δ − φ₁ vanishes outside K₁, ‖ψ_δ − φ₁‖₁ ≤ w(δ)·λ(K₁) ≤ η/2 for δ small, and ψ := ψ_δ works. ψ is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
4. (Convergence on ψ.) By hypothesis there is N with |∫ ψF_j dλ − ∫ ψF dλ| < ε/2 for every j ≥ N.
5. (Three-term estimate.) Let j ≥ N; all products below are integrable by step 1. By linearity, ∫ φF_j − ∫ φF = ∫ (φ − ψ)F_j − ∫ (φ − ψ)F + (∫ ψF_j − ∫ ψF). By step 1 each of the first two terms has absolute value at most C·‖φ − ψ‖₁ ≤ C·η < ε/4. Hence |∫ φF_j − ∫ φF| < ε/4 + ε/4 + ε/2 = ε.
6. (Conclusion.) ε > 0 was arbitrary, so ∫ φF_j dλ → ∫ φF dλ.
proof_key_steps: |∫ θG| ≤ C‖θ‖₁ for integrable θ and |G| ≤ C.
Approximate φ in L¹ by a C^∞ compactly supported ψ with ‖φ − ψ‖₁ ≤ ε/(4C + 1) (C_c density, then mollification).
Convergence on ψ holds by hypothesis.
Three-term estimate: |∫φF_j − ∫φF| ≤ 2C‖φ − ψ‖₁ + |∫ψF_j − ∫ψF| < ε for large j.

subproblems.title: Integration by parts for Jacobian minors of C² maps via the Piola identity, formula (3) for smooth maps (reused accepted lemma; supplied steps 3–5)
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ, let g_c : ℝ^k → ℝ (c ∈ Fin(r+1)) be of class C² (ContDiff ℝ 2), let V_b ∈ ℝ^k (b ∈ Fin(r+1)), and let ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ be of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1) with compact support. Here ℝ^k = Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure λ and D = fderiv ℝ. Let A(x) := (Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (row c, column b). For b ∈ Fin(r+1) let M_b(x) := det(Dg_{c+1}(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}, where s_b := Fin.succAbove b; this is the minor of A(x) without row 0 and column b. Then ∫ ψ(x)·det A(x) dλ(x) = −Σ_{b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (−1)^b ∫ Dψ(x)V_b·g_0(x)·M_b(x) dλ(x). (Reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_smooth_minor_ibp, whose frozen type is byte-identical.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (g : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k) (ψ : Euclid k → ℝ), (∀ c, ContDiff ℝ 2 (g c)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∫ x, ψ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b)) = -∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * ∫ x, fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun (c b' : Fin r) => fderiv ℝ (g c.succ) x (V (b.succAbove b')))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 (Laplace expansion), 4 (Piola identity) and 5 (integration by parts for smooth maps) of the supplied proof. They are stated with scalar rows g_c (the supplied v^{a(c)}) and arbitrary directions V_b (the supplied e_{b(t)}). The supplied hypotheses v ∈ C^∞ and φ ∈ C_c^∞ are weakened to g_c ∈ C² and ψ ∈ C_c^1, which is all that steps 3–5 use. This is the classical divergence form of a minor of a gradient, i.e. the Piola identity that the rows of a cofactor matrix are divergence free (L. C. Evans, Partial Differential Equations, §8.1.4; J. M. Ball, J. C. Currie, P. J. Olver, Null Lagrangians, weak continuity, and variational problems of arbitrary order, J. Funct. Anal. 41 (1981) 135–174). This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_smooth_minor_ibp (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.smooth_minor_ibp-a1, candidate commit dc9dd4b6139267dee9bdebebc5eb8b55f2c14e0d), reused with a byte-identical frozen type, so no new formal work is needed. Its accepted history already contains the accepted Piola identity Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_piola_identity (the content of step 3 below). The argument is the following.

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_W F(x) := DF(x)W; s_b := Fin.succAbove b : Fin r → Fin(r+1), the increasing enumeration of Fin(r+1) ∖ {b}; A(x) := (Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)}; h_c := g_{c+1} for c ∈ Fin r; M_b(x) := det(Dh_c(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}.

1. (Laplace expansion; supplied step 3.) Expanding along row 0 (Matrix.det_succ_row_zero), det A(x) = Σ_{b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (−1)^b·A(x)_{0,b}·det(A(x) without row 0 and column b) = Σ_b (−1)^b·∂_{V_b}g_0(x)·M_b(x). Indeed, deleting row 0 and column b of A(x) leaves the matrix (∂_{V_{s_b(b')}}g_{c+1}(x))_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}.
2. (Regularity.) Since g_c ∈ C², the map y ↦ Dg_c(y) is C¹ (ContDiff.fderiv_right). So every entry y ↦ ∂_W g_c(y) is C¹, in particular continuous. A determinant is a polynomial in its entries (Leibniz formula), so det A and every M_b are C¹. Hence F_b := ψ·g_0·M_b is C¹, and it vanishes outside the compact support of ψ.
3. (Piola identity; supplied step 4.) Claim: Σ_{b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (−1)^b·∂_{V_b}M_b(x) = 0 for every x ∈ ℝ^k.
   (a) Symmetry. For c ∈ Fin r and U, W ∈ ℝ^k the function E_c^W(y) := ∂_W h_c(y) is C¹ with ∂_U E_c^W(y) = D²h_c(y)(U)(W) =: H_c(y)(U, W). Since h_c is C², H_c(y)(U, W) = H_c(y)(W, U) (Schwarz; Mathlib ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt).
   (b) If r = 0, every M_b is the determinant of the empty matrix, the constant 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty). Its derivative vanishes and the claim holds. Let r ≥ 1.
   (c) Derivative of a determinant. Fix b and x and let N_b := (E_{c'}^{V_{s_b(b')}}(x))_{c',b' ∈ Fin r}, so M_b(x) = det N_b. Differentiating the Leibniz formula with the product rule gives ∂_{V_b}M_b(x) = Σ_{c ∈ Fin r} det N_b^{(c)}. Here N_b^{(c)} is N_b with its row c replaced by (H_c(x)(V_b, V_{s_b(b')}))_{b' ∈ Fin r}.
   (d) Expansion along the differentiated row. Let E be the r×(r+1) matrix E_{c',e} := E_{c'}^{V_e}(x). For distinct e, d ∈ Fin(r+1) let C_c(e, d) be the determinant of the (r−1)×(r−1) matrix obtained from E by deleting row c and the columns e and d, keeping the order of the remaining rows and columns; clearly C_c(e, d) = C_c(d, e). Deleting row c and column b' of N_b^{(c)} leaves the rows c' ≠ c of E restricted to the columns s_b(b''), b'' ≠ b'. Since s_b is increasing, these are the columns of E other than b and s_b(b'), in increasing order. So the Laplace expansion along row c gives det N_b^{(c)} = Σ_{b' ∈ Fin r} (−1)^{c+b'}·H_c(x)(V_b, V_{s_b(b')})·C_c(b, s_b(b')).
   (e) Reindexing. As b' runs over Fin r, d := s_b(b') runs over Fin(r+1) ∖ {b}, and b' = π_b(d), where π_b(d) := d if d < b and π_b(d) := d − 1 if d > b. Hence Σ_b (−1)^b det N_b^{(c)} = Σ_{b ≠ d} (−1)^{b+c+π_b(d)}·H_c(x)(V_b, V_d)·C_c(b, d), summed over ordered pairs of distinct elements of Fin(r+1).
   (f) Cancellation. Let b < d. The term (b, d) has sign (−1)^{b+c+d−1}, since π_b(d) = d − 1. The term (d, b) has sign (−1)^{d+c+b}, since π_d(b) = b. The signs are opposite, H_c(x)(V_b, V_d) = H_c(x)(V_d, V_b) by (a), and C_c(b, d) = C_c(d, b). So the two terms cancel, and Σ_b (−1)^b det N_b^{(c)} = 0 for every c. Summing over c and using (c) proves the claim. For r = 1 the C_c are empty determinants equal to 1, and (c)–(f) apply unchanged.
4. (Product rule.) For every x, ∂_{V_b}F_b(x) = ∂_{V_b}ψ(x)·g_0(x)·M_b(x) + ψ(x)·∂_{V_b}g_0(x)·M_b(x) + ψ(x)·g_0(x)·∂_{V_b}M_b(x).
5. (Pointwise identity.) Multiply step 4 by (−1)^b and sum over b. The middle terms add up to ψ·det A by step 1. The last terms add up to ψ·g_0·Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}M_b = 0 by step 3. Hence ψ(x)·det A(x) = Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}F_b(x) − Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}ψ(x)·g_0(x)·M_b(x) for every x.
6. (Exact derivatives integrate to zero; supplied step 5.) Let F : ℝ^k → ℝ be C¹ with compact support S, and let W ∈ ℝ^k. For τ ≠ 0, ∫ (F(u + τW) − F(u))/τ dλ(u) = 0, because ∫ F(u + τW) dλ(u) = ∫ F dλ by translation invariance of λ. As τ → 0 the integrand tends to ∂_W F(u) for every u. DF is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some B_F. The mean value inequality gives |F(u + τW) − F(u)|/|τ| ≤ B_F·‖W‖, and for |τ| ≤ 1 the integrand vanishes outside the compact set {u : dist(u, S) ≤ ‖W‖}. Dominated convergence along τ = 1/(n+1) gives ∫ ∂_W F dλ = 0.
7. (Integration.) All functions in step 5 are continuous with compact support, hence integrable: ∂_{V_b}ψ vanishes outside the support of ψ, and ∂_{V_b}F_b vanishes outside the support of F_b. Integrate step 5 and use linearity and step 6 for each F_b. This gives ∫ ψ·det A dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ, which is the claim, since ∂_{V_b}ψ(x) = Dψ(x)V_b.
proof_key_steps: Laplace expansion along row 0: det A = Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}g_0·M_b.
Piola identity Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}M_b = 0: differentiate each minor row by row, expand along the differentiated row, and cancel the terms (b, d) and (d, b) by symmetry of second derivatives.
The product rule for F_b := ψ g_0 M_b gives ψ det A = Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}F_b − Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}ψ g_0 M_b pointwise.
∫ ∂_W F = 0 for C¹ compactly supported F (translation invariance and dominated convergence); integrate.

subproblems.title: Smooth approximation of a Lipschitz function with the same Lipschitz constant, uniform convergence and a.e. convergence of derivatives (reused accepted lemma; supplied step 6(i)–(v))
subproblems.statement: Let k ∈ ℕ and L ∈ ℝ≥0, and let f : ℝ^k → ℝ be L-Lipschitz, where ℝ^k = Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure λ. Then there are functions f_n : ℝ^k → ℝ (n ∈ ℕ) such that every f_n is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞), the smooth class ∞), every f_n is L-Lipschitz, f_n → f uniformly on ℝ^k, and Df_n(x) → Df(x) in operator norm for λ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^k. Here D = fderiv ℝ, and Df(x) = 0 where f is not differentiable. (Reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_smooth_approx, whose frozen type is byte-identical.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ fs : ℕ → Euclid k → ℝ, (∀ n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fs n)) ∧ (∀ n, LipschitzWith L (fs n)) ∧ TendstoUniformly fs f atTop ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid k)), Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (fs n) x) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ f x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6(i)–(v) of the supplied proof (mollification v_δ := v ∗ ρ_δ along δ_ℓ → 0), stated for one scalar function f, which plays a coordinate v^i. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_smooth_approx (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.lipschitz_smooth_approx-a1, candidate commit ca73d99e39b455a43df67388b0f447d52245edef), reused with a byte-identical frozen type, so no new formal work is needed. Its accepted history already contains the accepted mollification lemmas Submission.cmcs_ls_mollify_lipschitz (step 3 below) and Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_mollify_fderiv_eq (step 5 below). The argument is the following.

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin k); B(x, R) is the open and B̄(x, R) the closed ball; ω := λ(B̄(0, 1)) ∈ (0, ∞), so λ(B̄(x, R)) = R^k·ω for R > 0.

1. (Kernels.) For n ∈ ℕ let R_n := 2/(n+2), so R_n → 0. Let φ_n be a smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius R_n/2 and outer radius R_n (Mathlib ContDiffBump). So φ_n is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ_n ≤ 1, φ_n = 1 on B̄(0, R_n/2), and φ_n vanishes outside B(0, R_n). Then I_n := ∫ φ_n dλ ≥ λ(B̄(0, R_n/2)) = (R_n/2)^k·ω > 0. Put ρ_n := φ_n/I_n. Then ρ_n is C^∞, ρ_n ≥ 0, ∫ ρ_n dλ = 1, ρ_n vanishes outside B(0, R_n) and has compact support, and ρ_n ≤ 1/I_n ≤ 2^k/(R_n^k·ω) = 2^k/λ(B̄(x, R_n)) for every x. Define f_n(x) := ∫ ρ_n(t)·f(x − t) dλ(t). For each x the integrand is continuous, since f is Lipschitz, and vanishes outside spt ρ_n, so it is integrable.
2. (Smoothness; step 6(i).) ρ_n is C^∞ with compact support, and f is continuous, hence locally integrable. So the convolution f_n = ρ_n ⋆ f is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
3. (Lipschitz constant; step 6(ii).) For x, x' ∈ ℝ^k, f_n(x) − f_n(x') = ∫ ρ_n(t)·(f(x − t) − f(x' − t)) dλ(t). Since ρ_n ≥ 0 and f is L-Lipschitz, |ρ_n(t)·(f(x − t) − f(x' − t))| ≤ ρ_n(t)·L·|x − x'|. Integrating with ∫ ρ_n = 1 gives |f_n(x) − f_n(x')| ≤ L·|x − x'|, so f_n is L-Lipschitz.
4. (Uniform convergence; step 6(iii).) Let x ∈ ℝ^k. Since ∫ ρ_n = 1, ρ_n ≥ 0 and ρ_n(t) = 0 for |t| ≥ R_n, |f_n(x) − f(x)| = |∫ ρ_n(t)·(f(x − t) − f(x)) dλ(t)| ≤ ∫ ρ_n(t)·L·|t| dλ(t) ≤ L·R_n. The bound L·R_n → 0 does not depend on x, so f_n → f uniformly on ℝ^k.
5. (Derivatives; step 6(iv).) Fix x, v ∈ ℝ^k. The substitution t = y − s, under which λ is invariant, gives f_n(y) = ∫ ρ_n(y − s)·f(s) dλ(s). For each s, y ↦ ρ_n(y − s)·f(s) is C¹ with derivative Dρ_n(y − s)·f(s). Dρ_n is continuous with compact support. So for |y − x| ≤ 1 these derivatives are bounded by sup‖Dρ_n‖·|f(s)| times the indicator of the compact set {s : dist(x − s, spt ρ_n) ≤ 1}, an integrable function of s. Differentiation under the integral sign (dominated convergence; Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left) gives Df_n(x)v = ∫ Dρ_n(x − s)v·f(s) dλ(s). Now h(s) := ρ_n(x − s) is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz, and Dh(s)(−v) = Dρ_n(x − s)v. Two facts finish the step. First, the Lipschitz integration-by-parts formula ∫ ∂_v f·h dλ = ∫ f·∂_{−v}h dλ (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq). It follows from ∫ ((f(s + τv) − f(s))/τ)·h(s) ds = ∫ f(s)·((h(s − τv) − h(s))/τ) ds, which holds by translation invariance, and dominated convergence as τ → 0. Second, Rademacher's theorem: f is differentiable λ-a.e., and ∂_v f(s) = Df(s)v there (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). Together they give ∫ Df(s)v·ρ_n(x − s) dλ(s) = ∫ Dρ_n(x − s)v·f(s) dλ(s). Hence Df_n(x)v = ∫ ρ_n(x − s)·Df(s)v dλ(s).
6. (A.e. convergence in a basis direction; step 6(v).) Fix i ∈ Fin k and put G(y) := Df(y)e_i. G is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv) and |G(y)| ≤ ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so G is locally integrable. λ is a doubling measure, so by the Lebesgue differentiation theorem (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), for λ-a.e. x the averages ⨍_{B̄(x, R)} |G(y) − G(x)| dλ(y) tend to 0 as R → 0⁺, in particular along R = R_n. Fix such an x. Note ∫ ρ_n(x − y) dλ(y) = 1 and ρ_n(x − y) = 0 for y ∉ B(x, R_n). So steps 5 and 1 give |Df_n(x)e_i − G(x)| = |∫ ρ_n(x − y)·(G(y) − G(x)) dλ(y)| ≤ (2^k/λ(B̄(x, R_n)))·∫_{B̄(x, R_n)} |G(y) − G(x)| dλ(y) = 2^k·⨍_{B̄(x, R_n)} |G − G(x)| dλ → 0. Mathlib packages this estimate as ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable, the ratio of outer to inner radius being 2. Hence Df_n(x)e_i → Df(x)e_i for λ-a.e. x.
7. (All basis directions.) Fin k is finite. So after discarding the union of the k exceptional null sets (ae_all_iff), there is a set of full measure on which Df_n(x)e_i → Df(x)e_i for every i.
8. (Operator norm.) Let T : ℝ^k → ℝ be continuous linear and w ∈ ℝ^k. Then w = Σ_i w_i e_i with |w_i| ≤ ‖w‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le), so |Tw| ≤ (Σ_i |Te_i|)·‖w‖. Hence ‖T‖ ≤ Σ_i |Te_i| (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). Take T = Df_n(x) − Df(x) at a point x of step 7: ‖Df_n(x) − Df(x)‖ ≤ Σ_i |Df_n(x)e_i − Df(x)e_i| → 0. So Df_n(x) → Df(x) for λ-a.e. x.
Steps 2, 3, 4 and 8 give the four required properties of the f_n.
proof_key_steps: Normalized bumps ρ_n supported in B(0, 2/(n+2)) with ρ_n ≤ 2^k/λ(B̄(x, 2/(n+2))); f_n := ρ_n ⋆ f is C^∞.
f_n is L-Lipschitz (∫ρ_n = 1, ρ_n ≥ 0), and |f_n − f| ≤ L·2/(n+2) uniformly.
Df_n(x)v = ∫ ρ_n(x − y)Df(y)v dy (differentiation under the integral, Lipschitz integration by parts, Rademacher); Lebesgue differentiation gives a.e. convergence to Df(x)v.
Apply this to the k basis vectors and use ‖T‖ ≤ Σ_i |Te_i| to get Df_n(x) → Df(x) for a.e. x.

subproblems.title: Integration by parts for Jacobian minors of Lipschitz maps, formula (3) for Lipschitz maps (reused accepted lemma; supplied step 6)
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ and L ∈ ℝ≥0, let g_c : ℝ^k → ℝ (c ∈ Fin(r+1)) be L-Lipschitz, let V_b ∈ ℝ^k (b ∈ Fin(r+1)), and let ψ : ℝ^k → ℝ be of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1) with compact support. Here ℝ^k = Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure λ, and D = fderiv ℝ is the zero map at non-differentiability points. Let A(x) := (Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (row c, column b) and M_b(x) := det(Dg_{c+1}(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}, where s_b := Fin.succAbove b. Then ∫ ψ(x)·det A(x) dλ(x) = −Σ_{b ∈ Fin(r+1)} (−1)^b ∫ Dψ(x)V_b·g_0(x)·M_b(x) dλ(x). (Reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_minor_ibp, whose frozen type is byte-identical.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (g : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin (r + 1) → Euclid k) (ψ : Euclid k → ℝ), (∀ c, LipschitzWith L (g c)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∫ x, ψ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b)) = -∑ b : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (b : ℕ) * ∫ x, fderiv ℝ ψ x (V b) * g 0 x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun (c b' : Fin r) => fderiv ℝ (g c.succ) x (V (b.succAbove b')))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the supplied proof, its last paragraph: "Apply (3) to v_{δ_ℓ} (step 5). Both sides converge by dominated convergence: all integrands vanish outside the compact set spt φ and are uniformly bounded there ... This gives (3) for v." It is stated for scalar L-Lipschitz rows g_c (the supplied v^{a(c)}), directions V_b (the supplied e_{b(t)}) and a C¹ compactly supported weight ψ. The mollified rows come from the sibling lipschitz_smooth_approx (supplied step 6(i)–(v)), formula (3) for smooth rows from the sibling smooth_minor_ibp (supplied steps 3–5), and the measurability and the uniform bounds K_r, K_{r−1} from the sibling minor_bound. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_minor_ibp (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.flat_convergence-a1.deformation-a1.jacobian_weak_continuity-a1.lipschitz_minor_ibp-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 7c2f0c43f702d533b42063c5e3634e4e453253cb), reused with a byte-identical frozen type, so no new formal work is needed. Its accepted Lean proof follows steps 1–7 below: it obtains the approximating rows from lipschitz_smooth_approx, applies smooth_minor_ibp for every n, and passes to the limit on both sides by dominated convergence with the measurability and bounds of minor_bound.

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_Wψ(x) := Dψ(x)W; s_b := Fin.succAbove b. For rows h = (h_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} put A[h](x) := (Dh_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin(r+1)} and M_b[h](x) := det(Dh_{c+1}(x)V_{s_b(b')})_{c,b' ∈ Fin r}. Put B := (r+1)!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^{r+1} and, for b ∈ Fin(r+1), B_b := r!·(L·Σ_{b' ∈ Fin r} ‖V_{s_b(b')}‖)^r.

1. (Approximation.) For each c ∈ Fin(r+1), the sibling lipschitz_smooth_approx, applied to the L-Lipschitz g_c, gives functions g^n_c (n ∈ ℕ) that are C^∞ and L-Lipschitz. They satisfy g^n_c → g_c uniformly on ℝ^k, and Dg^n_c(x) → Dg_c(x) for all x outside a λ-null set N_c. The finite union N := ∪_c N_c is λ-null. Write g^n := (g^n_c)_c.
2. (Smooth identity.) For every n the g^n_c are C^∞, hence C², and ψ is C¹ with compact support. So the sibling smooth_minor_ibp gives ∫ ψ·det A[g^n] dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^n_0·M_b[g^n] dλ for every n.
3. (Pointwise convergence.) Let x ∉ N. For all c and every direction W, Dg^n_c(x)W → Dg_c(x)W, since evaluation at W is continuous on the space of continuous linear maps. The determinant is a continuous (polynomial) function of the entries. So det A[g^n](x) → det A[g](x) and M_b[g^n](x) → M_b[g](x) for every b. Moreover g^n_0(x) → g_0(x) for every x.
4. (Measurability and bounds.) All g^n_c are L-Lipschitz. Apply the sibling minor_bound to the rows (g^n_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} with the directions V, and to the rows (g^n_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r} with the directions V ∘ s_b. So det A[g^n] and M_b[g^n] are measurable, with |det A[g^n](x)| ≤ B and |M_b[g^n](x)| ≤ B_b for all n and x. ψ is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Dψ is continuous because ψ ∈ C¹, and it vanishes outside the support of ψ, so ∂_{V_b}ψ is continuous with compact support. The g^n_0 and g_0 are continuous.
5. (Left side.) |ψ·det A[g^n]| ≤ B·|ψ|, an integrable function independent of n. The integrands are measurable, and ψ·det A[g^n] → ψ·det A[g] on ℝ^k ∖ N by step 3. By dominated convergence, ∫ ψ·det A[g^n] dλ → ∫ ψ·det A[g] dλ.
6. (Right side.) By uniform convergence there is n_0 with |g^n_0(x) − g_0(x)| ≤ 1 for all x and all n ≥ n_0. For n ≥ n_0 and every x, |∂_{V_b}ψ(x)·g^n_0(x)·M_b[g^n](x)| ≤ B_b·|∂_{V_b}ψ(x)|·(|g_0(x)| + 1). This bound is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. The integrands are measurable (step 4) and converge on ℝ^k ∖ N to ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b[g] (step 3). Dominated convergence, with a bound valid for all n ≥ n_0, gives ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^n_0·M_b[g^n] dλ → ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b[g] dλ for each b. The sum over b is finite, so the right side of step 2 converges to −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b[g] dλ.
7. (Conclusion.) The two sides of step 2 are equal for every n, so their limits from steps 5 and 6 are equal, since limits in ℝ are unique. This is the claimed identity ∫ ψ·det A[g] dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ Dψ(x)V_b·g_0·M_b[g] dλ.
proof_key_steps: Approximate every row by C^∞, L-Lipschitz functions converging uniformly, with a.e. convergent derivatives (sibling lipschitz_smooth_approx).
For each n apply formula (3) for smooth rows (sibling smooth_minor_ibp).
Entries, hence determinants and minors, converge a.e.; minor_bound gives measurability and the uniform bounds B, B_b.
Dominated convergence on both sides (bounds B|ψ| and B_b|∂_{V_b}ψ|(|g_0| + 1) for n ≥ n_0), then uniqueness of limits.

subproblems.title: Weak continuity of Jacobian minors of scalar Lipschitz rows under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants; the induction P(r) (supplied steps 2 and 7)
subproblems.statement: Let k, r ∈ ℕ and L ∈ ℝ≥0. For j ∈ ℕ and c ∈ Fin r let g^j_c, g_c : ℝ^k → ℝ be L-Lipschitz, with g^j_c → g_c uniformly on ℝ^k as j → ∞ for every c. Let V_b ∈ ℝ^k (b ∈ Fin r), and let φ : ℝ^k → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable. Here ℝ^k = Euclid k carries Lebesgue measure λ, and Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x is the zero map at points where g is not differentiable. Then ∫ φ(x)·det(Dg^j_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin r} dλ(x) → ∫ φ(x)·det(Dg_c(x)V_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin r} dλ(x) as j → ∞ (row c, column b).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (k r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (gs : ℕ → Fin r → Euclid k → ℝ) (g : Fin r → Euclid k → ℝ) (V : Fin r → Euclid k) (φ : Euclid k → ℝ), Integrable φ → (∀ j c, LipschitzWith L (gs j c)) → (∀ c, LipschitzWith L (g c)) → (∀ c, TendstoUniformly (fun j => gs j c) (g c) atTop) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, φ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (gs j c) x (V b))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, φ x * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => fderiv ℝ (g c) x (V b))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof (the induction P(r)), together with its step 2 (reduction to smooth compactly supported weights). It is written for scalar L-Lipschitz rows g_c and arbitrary directions V_b. For the coordinate rows g_c = v^{a(c)} and the directions V_t = e_{b(t)} these minors agree a.e. with the supplied M^{a,b}(v) (supplied Notation; this identification is done in the parent). The three siblings used are reused comparator-accepted declarations: minor_bound = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_minor_measurable_bound (the bound K_r of the supplied Notation and step 1), weak_star_l1_upgrade = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_weak_star_l1_upgrade (supplied step 2), and lipschitz_minor_ibp = Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_lipschitz_minor_ibp (formula (3) of supplied step 6). The supplied terms T1_{j,t} and T2_{j,t} are the error term and the induction term of steps 5 and 6 below. This is the classical weak continuity of minors, i.e. of null Lagrangians (Morrey, Reshetnyak; Ball 1977; J. M. Ball, J. C. Currie, P. J. Olver, Null Lagrangians, weak continuity, and variational problems of arbitrary order, J. Funct. Anal. 41 (1981) 135–174).

Notation: λ = volume on ℝ^k = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_Wψ(x) := Dψ(x)W; s_b := Fin.succAbove b : Fin r → Fin(r+1), the increasing enumeration of Fin(r+1) ∖ {b}. For m ∈ ℕ, rows h = (h_c)_{c ∈ Fin m} and directions W = (W_b)_{b ∈ Fin m} put J(h, W)(x) := det(Dh_c(x)W_b)_{c,b ∈ Fin m} (row c, column b). P(r) is the statement: for all L ∈ ℝ≥0, all families g^j = (g^j_c)_{c ∈ Fin r} (j ∈ ℕ) and g = (g_c)_{c ∈ Fin r} of L-Lipschitz functions with g^j_c → g_c uniformly for every c, all W ∈ (ℝ^k)^r and all integrable φ, ∫ φ·J(g^j, W) dλ → ∫ φ·J(g, W) dλ. We prove P(r) by induction on r, for all these data simultaneously (in Lean: induction on r after introducing only k and r, so that the induction hypothesis is quantified over L, the rows, the directions and the weight). P(r) for the given r is the claim.

1. (Base case r = 0.) The determinant of the empty matrix is 1 (Matrix.det_isEmpty). So both integrals equal ∫ φ dλ for every j, and a constant sequence converges (tendsto_const_nhds).
2. (Step r → r + 1: reduction to smooth weights.) Assume P(r). Let g^j, g be families indexed by Fin(r+1) as in the statement, let V ∈ (ℝ^k)^{r+1}, and put D_j := J(g^j, V) and D := J(g, V). The sibling minor_bound, applied to the rows g^j (for each j) and to the rows g with the directions V, shows that D_j and D are measurable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, and that |D_j(x)| ≤ B and |D(x)| ≤ B for all j and x, where B := (r+1)!·(L·Σ_b ‖V_b‖)^{r+1}. By the sibling weak_star_l1_upgrade with C := B, F_j := D_j and F := D, it therefore suffices to show ∫ ψ·D_j dλ → ∫ ψ·D dλ for every C^∞ function ψ with compact support (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ and HasCompactSupport ψ).
3. (Integration by parts; supplied step 6.) Fix such a ψ. It is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le, since 1 ≤ ∞). Put M^j_b := J((g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, V ∘ s_b) and M_b := J((g_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, V ∘ s_b) for b ∈ Fin(r+1). The sibling lipschitz_minor_ibp, applied to the L-Lipschitz rows (g^j_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} and to the L-Lipschitz rows (g_c)_{c ∈ Fin(r+1)} with the directions V and the weight ψ, gives ∫ ψ·D_j dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ and ∫ ψ·D dλ = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ. Negation, finite sums and multiplication by the constants (−1)^b preserve limits (Tendsto.neg, tendsto_finsetSum, Tendsto.const_mul). So it suffices to prove ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ → ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ for each b ∈ Fin(r+1).
4. (Splitting.) Fix b. The function χ_b := ∂_{V_b}ψ, x ↦ Dψ(x)V_b, is continuous, because ψ is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv composed with evaluation at V_b), and it vanishes outside the support of ψ, so it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv); hence it is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). The functions g^j_0 and g_0 are continuous, being Lipschitz. Put θ_b := χ_b·g_0; it is continuous with compact support, hence integrable, and so is χ_b·g^j_0. By minor_bound, applied to the rows (g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r} with the directions V ∘ s_b, M^j_b is measurable with |M^j_b(x)| ≤ B_b := r!·(L·Σ_{b' ∈ Fin r} ‖V_{s_b(b')}‖)^r for all j and x. A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function times an integrable function is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul), so θ_b·M^j_b and χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b are integrable, hence so is their difference χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b. By linearity of the integral (integral_add), ∫ χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ = ∫ χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b dλ + ∫ θ_b·M^j_b dλ for every j.
5. (Error term T1.) Let ε > 0 and put K := B_b·∫ |χ_b| dλ + 1 > 0. By the uniform convergence g^j_0 → g_0 (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff) there is N with |g^j_0(x) − g_0(x)| < ε/(2K) for all x and all j ≥ N. For such j and every x, |χ_b(x)·(g^j_0(x) − g_0(x))·M^j_b(x)| ≤ (ε/(2K))·B_b·|χ_b(x)|. Integrating (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le) gives |∫ χ_b·(g^j_0 − g_0)·M^j_b dλ| ≤ (ε/(2K))·B_b·∫ |χ_b| dλ ≤ (ε/(2K))·K = ε/2 < ε. Hence this term tends to 0 as j → ∞.
6. (Induction term T2.) The functions g^j_{c+1} and g_{c+1} (c ∈ Fin r) are L-Lipschitz, with g^j_{c+1} → g_{c+1} uniformly for every c. So P(r), applied to the families (g^j_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r} and (g_{c+1})_{c ∈ Fin r}, the directions V ∘ s_b and the integrable weight θ_b from step 4, gives ∫ θ_b·M^j_b dλ → ∫ θ_b·M_b dλ.
7. (Conclusion of the step.) By steps 4–6 and the sum rule for limits (Tendsto.add), ∫ χ_b·g^j_0·M^j_b dλ → 0 + ∫ θ_b·M_b dλ = ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b dλ for every b. By step 3, ∫ ψ·D_j dλ → ∫ ψ·D dλ for every C^∞ compactly supported ψ, and by step 2, ∫ φ·D_j dλ → ∫ φ·D dλ for every integrable φ. This proves P(r+1) and completes the induction.
